What's Your Game: Already won a hurdle; can repeat that ability. Carries 7 lb more and jumped/hung imperfectly.
original_pre_race_assessment.why_verdict_survives: Several relevant performances already exist at the same basic weights. They justify opposition while allowing Sea The Day to improve. Herbies Sock is further demonstrated opposition, not a co-equal principal after a distant second.

original_pre_race_assessment.summary: Lejo Du Seuil brings a recent fourth in a stronger handicap; Lully Du Houx has already won on testing ground. The favourite's case rests more on further progress.
original_pre_race_assessment.counterargument: Two placed junior-hurdle runs, a potentially workable opening mark, a new Skelton yard and a longer trip offer a coherent improvement route. Fitness and stamina remain unknown.
original_pre_race_assessment.rival_limitations: Lejo Du Seuil: Recent Newbury handicap fourth; same 158 lb effective weight and a class drop. Longer trip still requires transfer. Lully Du Houx: Recent heavy-ground handicap winner; 157 lb. Up 6 lb and has yet to demonstrate this longer trip. Crystal Orchard: Recent hurdle second and Exeter third; 156 lb. Has jumping flaws and still needs handicap improvement.
original_pre_race_assessment.why_verdict_survives: The first two supply concrete competitive evidence. The 1 lb rating difference between Majeur and Lejo is effectively accommodated by the age/weight terms, not a free advantage. Do not count Crystal's speculative improvement equally.

original_pre_race_assessment.counterargument: He made all and jumped well at Warwick; improved consistency and an easy win mean he may have more in hand than the bare mark.

Star Of Affinity: Recent chase winner; same 167 lb despite a 118 versus 111 base rating. Up 4 lb and made jumping errors.
original_pre_race_assessment.why_verdict_survives: These rivals have relevant chase evidence, with less favourable penalty treatment for Yes Day. His own improvement remains consequential, but the field is materially stronger. Muskoka, Diplomatic Ash and Royal Time were reviewed too.
